title: Documents, Layout & Tables
description: Study ocr and layout preservation, table structure and units, charts and visual uncertainty, and document evidence and citations. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: OCR and layout preservation
lessons.description: Sketch a block-based reading order and a low-confidence OCR review rule.
lessons.conceptOverview: OCR produces text estimates, often with bounding boxes and confidence. Reading order, columns and headings must be reconstructed before chunking or a correct word stream can still yield an incorrect document meaning.
lessons.whyItMatters: Document structure must survive text extraction.

lessons.title: Table structure and units
lessons.description: Represent one table cell with its row, column, unit and page reference.
lessons.conceptOverview: Tables encode meaning through row headers, column headers, merged cells and units. Store that structure alongside values and retain the source location; isolated numeric chunks lose the relationships needed to answer questions.
lessons.whyItMatters: Numeric retrieval needs headers and units.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Tables encode meaning through row headers, column headers, merged cells and units. Store that structure alongside values and retain the source location; isolated numeric chunks lose the relationships needed to answer questions.

sections.title: Concept
sections.content: Tables encode meaning through row headers, column headers, merged cells and units. Store that structure alongside values and retain the source location; isolated numeric chunks lose the relationships needed to answer questions.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A revenue table labels its columns in thousands. An extracted value of 125 is incorrectly reported as 125 dollars instead of 125 thousand dollars.

sections.title: Practice & verification
sections.content: Represent one table cell with its row, column, unit and page reference. Write down your reasoning and check it against the concept before continuing.

keyTakeaways: Numeric retrieval needs headers and units.
commonMistakes: The cell value alone is sufficient evidence for a financial answer.

lessons.title: Charts and visual uncertainty
lessons.description: Describe how to distinguish linear and logarithmic axes before estimating a midpoint.
lessons.conceptOverview: A chart may require legend matching, axis interpretation and approximate position reading. Truncated axes and logarithmic scales change interpretation. Report uncertainty when extracting values from pixels, and prefer underlying data when available.
lessons.whyItMatters: Read axis semantics before estimating values.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: A chart may require legend matching, axis interpretation and approximate position reading. Truncated axes and logarithmic scales change interpretation. Report uncertainty when extracting values from pixels, and prefer underlying data when available.

sections.title: Concept
sections.content: A chart may require legend matching, axis interpretation and approximate position reading. Truncated axes and logarithmic scales change interpretation. Report uncertainty when extracting values from pixels, and prefer underlying data when available.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A logarithmic axis places 10 and 100 one interval apart. Treating it as linear leads to incorrect interpolated values.

sections.title: Practice & verification
sections.content: Describe how to distinguish linear and logarithmic axes before estimating a midpoint. Write down your reasoning and check it against the concept before continuing.

keyTakeaways: Read axis semantics before estimating values.
commonMistakes: Equal vertical distances always represent equal numeric differences.

lessons.title: Document evidence and citations
lessons.description: Define an evidence record and a test that checks whether the cited region supports the answer.
lessons.conceptOverview: A useful document answer links each claim to a page and region or text span. Preserve extraction version and source identity so a citation can be replayed after reprocessing; page-level proximity alone does not prove support.
lessons.whyItMatters: Citations need supporting evidence, not just the correct document.

sections.title: Worked example
